newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-CSKA BRACE FOR ALANIA VISIT, CALL IN TROOPS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CSKA BRACE FOR ALANIA VISIT, CALL IN TROOPS.

text.p: CSKA Moscow, the Russian Army team, had to call in troops to clear 10 cm of snow from the pitch before Saturday's game against Alania Vladikavkaz.

Sadly for CSKA, reinforcements have been harder to find for the squad members who walked out in a close-season split. The team would be glad just to avoid defeat against Alania, who thumped KamAZ 5-0 in the opening game at Vladikavkaz on Sunday.
The army side looked out of sorts last weekend, losing their opening game 2-0 on the same ground to co-tenants, Dynamo.
The heavy snow which struck Moscow on Friday was a blow for Russian league bosses who have been lobbying clubs to bring the season into line with the rest of Europe.

Troops were also out at Lokomotiv's Cherkizovsky ground, where champions Spartak Moscow take on promoted Shinnik Yaroslavl, and staff were hoping for army help at Torpedo Moscow where Siberia's Dynamo-Gazovik Tyumen are the visitors on Saturday.

All three Moscow premier league grounds, shared by the capital's five clubs, have the undersoil heating made obligatory by the league this season. But it is little defence against heavy snow falling close to kick off.
Eight provincial sides were forced to play their opening home game at an away ground as punishment for failing to install heated pitches in time.
In Friday's games, KamAZ Naberzhniye Chelny played their "home" match at Vladikavkaz in southern Russia and were hammered 5-0 by Rotor Volgograd.
Baltika Kaliningrad beat Lokomotiv Nizhny Novogrod 1-0 at the neutral ground of Krasnodar while Fakel Voronezh lost 1-0 to Krylya Sovietov Samara in snow-free Novorossiisk.
Rostselmash Rostov will have to travel to Krasnodar on Saturday to play against Lokomotiv Moscow.
